summary: Embedding namespace migration produced cross-shard fanout and high rerank tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in end-to-end rerank latency after they performed a namespaced embedding migration last week. The reranker returns correct results but 99th percentile latency for batch rerank calls spikes to 6–9s (baseline ~300ms) and occasional 503s observed from the rerank endpoint.

Impact:
- Intermittent but customer-facing UX timeouts for search results in production (LexiSearch CDN observes >20% degraded sessions).
- Increased request retries causing downstream quota consumption.
- Supports enterprise SLA (high priority customer).

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east-1, dedicated project for LexiSearch (enterprise, VPC).
- Embeddings stored in namespaced index: "lexi_v2_migrated" and legacy namespace "lexi_v1" (migration executed 2026-03-05 03:10 UTC).
- Rerank route: /v1/rerank/batch -> routed to reranker-mini-1 behind router service.

Steps to reproduce (from customer guidance):
1) Call embedding upload API with namespace header set to "lexi_v2_migrated" (bulk ingest).
2) Trigger rerank endpoint using saved candidate ids referencing both namespaces (some documents still point to lex_v1 ids).
3) Observe higher tail latency and periodic 503s.

Observed behavior:
- Per-request traces show fanout to 3+ embed-store shard replicas for a single rerank request. We expect 1-2 shards based on sharding key.
- Router logs show repeated resolv/lookup queries for same document ids across namespaces, increasing I/O and queuing on embedding-store workers.
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 58% for customer's requests after migration.

Expected behavior:
- Deterministic routing to single shard per id and stable KV cache hit rate. Rerank p99 should remain below 800ms.

Initial logs & traces:
- Trace sample (request id 9b7f-...): router -> embed-store: lookup(keys: [d-143, d-144, d-712]) -> embed-store returned duplicate shard mapping: shards [shard-12, shard-18, shard-12] causing duplicate fetch attempts.
- Router debug: discovered two different namespace-to-shard mappings for "d-712" (lexi_v2_migrated -> shard-18, lexi_v1 -> shard-12). Migration script annotated some ids with both namespaces due to client-side duplicate-key retries.
- Metrics: embed-store queue depth +300% on shard-18 for a 30-minute window near migration completion.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Migration produced duplicate namespace labels on a subset (~0.6%) of document ids. When rerank receives mixed namespace candidate lists it attempts per-namespace resolution causing cross-shard fanout.
- Hypothesis 2: Router shard-mapping cache invalidation was delayed; stale mapping caused lookups to be sent to multiple shard endpoints until caches expired.
- We validated that embedding-store indexes contain duplicate keys across namespaces by running a sampling scan (internal tool: emb-index-inspect).
- Confirmed two client-side ingest retries (from LexiSearch bulk uploader) created duplicate records with slightly different metadata and namespace headers.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support enabled per-request namespace-coercion at the router for LexiSearch (forces lookup to prefer lexi_v2_migrated) — reduced fanout and dropped p99 from ~7s to ~1.2s for affected fleet. Applied 2026-03-11 02:40 UTC.
- Increased router shard-mapping cache TTL temporarily to avoid oscillation while we clean duplicates.

Next steps / recommended remediation:
1) Customer action: Run a dedupe job using customer-provided id map and the 'emb-index-clean' helper to remove duplicate keys in lexi_v1 that now also exist in lexi_v2_migrated. We provided a safe migration runbook link.
2) Infra action: Run targeted index compaction on shard-12 and shard-18 during low-traffic window (proposed 2026-03-13 01:00–03:00 UTC).
3) Router: Add hard check to prefer per-request namespace header and fall back only when explicit flag is set (postmortem change).
4) Engineering: Add validation to bulk-ingest client to detect duplicate-id retries and surface warnings.

Notes/links:
- Slack thread: #support-lexi (https://slack.redwood/support-lexis)
- Related PR: github.com/redwood/embeddings-service/pull/98 (namespace-coercion at router)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/namespace-migration-checklist

2026-03-10 14:35 UTC - SRE (Maya Chen): Confirmed shard queue buildup on shard-18; capturing queue metrics and taking conservative throttle snapshot.

2026-03-12 16:05 UTC - Miguel Santos: Scheduled compaction for shard-12 and shard-18 on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Will follow up with post-compaction metrics and rollback plan if any increased latency observed.

resolution: Mitigation in place: router-level namespace coercion reduced p99 from ~7s to ~1.2s. Scheduled index compaction and customer dedupe job. Pending engineering change to bulk-ingest validation and router preference logic. Will update to Resolved when compaction completes and p99 stabilizes under 800ms for 48h.
